prompt: An airline wants to cut operating costs by 10%. The candidate's framework: (1) Fuel costs; (2) Labor costs: pilots, crew and ground staff; (3) Aircraft ownership and maintenance; (4) Crew scheduling and staffing levels. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Missing: maintenance contracts with outside suppliers
options.feedback: Outside maintenance is part of bucket 3, aircraft ownership and maintenance.

options.text: Bucket 3 doesn't belong: aircraft are long-term commitments
options.feedback: Aircraft ownership and maintenance are among an airline's largest costs, and leases and maintenance schedules can be renegotiated. They belong in the cost tree.

options.text: Buckets 2 and 4 overlap: staffing levels drive labor cost
options.feedback: Right. Crew scheduling and staffing levels are how labor cost is managed, so bucket 4 repeats bucket 2. Use the slot for airport and navigation fees.

options.text: It's a generic cost tree: an airline is better cut by route than by cost line
options.feedback: Splitting cost by line is a valid, complete cut, and route detail can sit inside each line. The flaw is that bucket 4 repeats labor.

explanation: Staffing levels and scheduling are how labor cost is managed, so bucket 4 repeats bucket 2. A complete cost tree: fuel, labor, aircraft, airport and navigation fees, and overhead.

extras.corrected_framework: Fuel; labor; aircraft ownership and maintenance; airport and navigation fees; overhead
